title: Model routing + fallback incremental rollout playbook and weekmap
content:
Context and goal:

This doc is a working playbook for an incremental rollout of the new model-routing policy with layered fallbacks. Target deployment: hosted inference (api-redwood-us-east), Dedicated pools (dedicated-gpu-2), and Private vpc customer pilots.

Why this is different: model routing changes the runtime decisioning path (route->model-variant->fallback chain). We must protect latency SLOs (p50 < 70ms for short responses), avoid tail amplification during cascade fallbacks, and ensure quality regressions are visible quickly.

Primary objectives (MUST):
- Gradual traffic ramp of routing policy across 5 canary cohorts (0.1%, 1%, 5%, 20%, 100%).
- Validate fallback correctness (variant mapping, token-preserving fallback).
- Keep aggregate p95 below 250ms; immediate rollback if p95 > 400ms sustained for 5m.
- No customer-facing errors > 0.5% at cohort >5%.

Quick summary of the plan (weekmap):
- Day 0 (prep, Fri 2027-04-16): preflight runbook, smoke test, TTL cache warmup on dedicated pools, publish release-notes-draft to internal channels.
- Day 1 (Mon 2027-04-19): Canary cohort A (0.1%) — 180m observation window. Shift-watcher window: 09:00-12:00 PDT.
- Day 2 (Tue 2027-04-20): Canary cohort B (1%) — extend observation, run traffic sweep tests, begin synthetic prompt set for evals.
- Day 3 (Wed 2027-04-21): Canary cohort C (5%) — long-tail latency stress test, run explosive prompt fanout test (batching stress).
- Day 4 (Thu 2027-04-22): Canary cohort D (20%) — readiness gating for 100% rollout. Opt-in dedicated region for private pilots.
- Day 5 (Fri 2027-04-23): Full ramp to 100% with staged throttles (if all gates green). Post-roll notes and retro.

Preflight checklist (to be completed before Day 0):
- [ ] Merge gating PRs: runtime routing, routing-config API, feature-flag infra. Check github/pr 781 and 790 for hotfixes.
- [ ] Conflate model-variant table with catalog: ensure variant IDs are immutable for this rollout.
- [ ] Telemetry hooks: route_id, variant_id, fallback_reason, latency_ms, token_count must be emitted for every request.
- [ ] Canary config in routing-control plane created as: routing.policy.v1.canary-2027-04.
- [ ] Alerting: temporary alerts scoped to canaries created in PagerDuty (PD escalation policy: routing-canary).
- [ ] Load-tests: smoke (5qps), sustained read (200qps) against ded pool.
- [ ] KV cache warmup scripts scheduled for 30m prior to each cohort ramp.
- [ ] Ops playbook published to #release-orchestra slack and to runbook owner pager.

Run-time guardrails and thresholds (auto-checks):
- Error-rate: rollback immediate if 5m rolling error_rate > 0.5% (5000ppm) on any cohort >5% of traffic.
- Latency: p95 > 400ms for 5m => automatic circuit to previous routing config. p95 > 250ms sustained for 15m => manual check.
- Quality: model-choice regression (BLEU/embedding-sim over eval set) drop > 2% on canary cohort => halt and roll back.
- Fallback storm detection: if fallback_rate increases by > 3x baseline and correlates to increased downstream CPU/GPU saturation, start emergency throttle.

Manual checks during observation windows (watcher tasks):
- Shift watcher (primary): verify health in real-time dashboard, watch logs for 502/504 spikes, confirm variant mapping is stable.
- Observability lead: run quick SLO queries (p50/p95/p99) and token-cost delta vs baseline.
- ML lead: run 20-sample semantic diff against baseline for a random bucket of logs; check hallucination markers.
- Infra lead: check GPU utilization on dedicated pools, queue lengths for batchers.
- SRE: validate synthetic traffic baseline (prometheus synthetic probe run).

Communication plan (templates):
- Pre-announce: short note to #customer-ops and #gta: "Planned incremental rollout of model-routing; low risk, will monitor; contact PD routing-canary for issues."
- On escalation: ETA-based updates every 15m for first hour then 30m. Use template: SUMMARY / IMPACT / MITIGATION / NEXT STEPS.
- Post-roll: short release note (internal) + public-facing release blurb for KB if user-visible changes occurred.

Rollback and rollback matrix (fast paths):
- Fast rollback (config switch): move traffic back to `routing.policy.v0.stable` (instant; config plane). Post-mortem required if rollback triggered.
- Gradual unwind: reduce cohort multipliers (20% -> 5% -> 1% -> 0.1%) if partial instability but not catastrophic.
- Emergency kill: disable routing-control plane via admin toggle; fallback to model-pin mapping. Requires SRE and infra on call.

Telemetry and dashboards to watch (links to dashboards in linked_artifacts; dashboards must include):
- Canary routing dashboard: per-cohort p95/p99, error rate, fallback_rate, variant_hit_rate, request_count.
- Cost delta board: tokens per response vs baseline; GPU-hours delta on dedicated.
- Quality regression board: eval-set averaged metrics, embedding similarity deltas, small-sample diffs.

Safety experiments to run before cohort C (5%):
- Prefix-preserving fallback test: intentionally drop variant for synthetic keys and verify tokens/kv-cache semantics preserved.
- Batching backpressure test: ramp many short-lived requests to exercise batcher and verify latency tail does not spike.
- Region failover simulation: simulate us-east full capacity and validate automatic fallback to compatible model-variant in eu-west without data leakage.

Open questions / TODOs (owner tags inline):
- [PRIORITY] How to surface per-request routing-decisions to trace spans without blowing tracing volume? (Owner: Lena)
- [SECURITY] Confirm that fallback variants do not route to private-only models for public customers. (Owner: Priyanka)
- [OPS] Decide whether to include a temporary 1s client-side retry window for 503 -> fallback attempts. (Owner: Omar)
- [COST] Calculate expected token-cost delta for cohort D (Owner: Marcus)

Runbook checklist (concrete steps during a cohort increase):
1) Notify channels: #release-orchestra, #customer-ops, and PD routing-canary.
2) Set canary multiplier in routing-control to target percentage.
3) Kick off KV warmup job targeted at ded pools (watch logs).
4) Wait 180m or required observation window. During this time run the manual checks above every 30m.
5) If gates green, advance to next cohort. If any gate trips, follow rollback matrix.
6) After full ramp, enable extended telemetry retention for 7 days for post-roll analysis.

Draft release notes (internal -> edited for public):
- Title: "Incremental rollout: smarter model routing with deterministic fallbacks (Apr 2027)"
- Summary (internal): We shipped a routing-policy update that improves latency and reduces unit cost by routing short queries to smaller variants and failing over to higher-capacity variants only when needed. The rollout is gated and instrumented with canaries and fallback protections.
- What's changed (engineer-friendly): New routing-control plane config (routing.policy.v1.canary-2027-04); variant pinning semantics updated; prefix-preserving fallback.
- Impact: Expected lower median latency for short queries, small token-cost reduction for mixed workloads, transparent fallbacks for compatibility. No schema changes to API.
- Rollback plan: config switch to routing.policy.v0.stable. Contact: routing-canary PD.

Post-roll analysis checklist (after Day 5):
- [ ] Collate telemetry, produce a 48h and 7d summary: latency, error rates, variant-hit ratios, and cost delta.
- [ ] Run a 500-sample semantic diff and surface top 5 regression prompts.
- [ ] Owner retrospective: ops, infra, ml, product; capture lessons, update playbook.
- [ ] Create a small KB entry for customers if behavioral differences are visible.

Annex: quick command snippets (ops shortcuts):
- Set canary multiplier (example): curl -X POST https://routing-control/api/v1/canaries -d '{"name":"canary-2027-04","multiplier":0.01}' (ops shortcut, use internal curl wrapper).
- Rollback (config switch): routingctl set active-policy routing.policy.v0.stable --reason "auto-rollback p95"
- KV warmup launcher: /scripts/kv_warmup.sh --pool dedicated-gpu-2 --seed-list seeds/canary-keys.txt

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep early cohorts in business hours only; weekend ramping increases blast radius.
- Be conservative with telemetry sampling early; we want signal not noise.
- Remember to verify billing tags on requests for private pilots so we don't misattribute cost.

End of draft.
